inputs.last_fcf_justification: FY2025 FCF was +$1,187M, the first materially positive year as peak capex ($1.53B in FY2024) normalised toward $0.87B in FY2025 and guided $0.8-1.0B in FY2026. Historical median FCF is -$305M and is structurally misleading — FSLR was in a decade-long capacity buildout (Ohio x4, Alabama, Louisiana, India) with capex $0.9-1.5B/yr; the negative FCF reflects expansion investment, not earnings weakness. FY2025 net income $1,528M + D&A ~$350M - normalised capex ~$850M = ~$1,028M; FY2025 actual $1,187M. $1,200M rounded base is a conservative forward-normalised proxy aligned with FY2025 actuals and post-buildout steady state.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Mid-cycle owner FCF of $700m, NOT an observed figure -- H1-2026 free cash flow was NEGATIVE ~$639.6m (operating cash flow -$359.8m less capex $279.8m) against net income of $769.2m, a gap of roughly $1.13bn. The largest single driver is a $649.3m INCREASE in government grants receivable: First Solar is recognising Section 45X in earnings far faster than it collects it (non-current grants receivable rose $125.6m -> $978.8m). Any model converting earnings to cash at a stable ratio will materially overstate FCF. The prior model's $1,200m base with +15% Year-1 growth is unsupported.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Not computed: FCF was negative throughout FY2016-FY2024 due to deliberate capacity buildout capex cycle (peak $1.53B in FY2024). FY2025 is the first normalised positive FCF year. Historical FCF CAGR is structurally misleading and is replaced by forward-normalised FCF base of $1,200M.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_detail: Equity 5yr CAGR (11.56%) vs Revenue 5yr CAGR (14.00%): divergence 2.4pp — within tolerance. Equity 5yr vs EPS 5yr (30.67%): divergence 19.1pp — within 30pp threshold. EPS CAGR is elevated due to 45X credit ramp in FY2023-FY2025; equity CAGR selected as conservative anchor per value-investing methodology. Forward scenario growth rates reflect contracted backlog ramp, capacity expansion, and 45X credit trajectory rather than extrapolating historical equity CAGR linearly.

wacc_rationale: Base 11%. The risk is POLICY and CONCENTRATION, not cyclicality. Section 45X reduced H1 cost of sales by $862.5m -- 79.0% of H1 gross profit and 108.4% of H1 operating income; ex-45X, H1 operating income is NEGATIVE $66.8m and Q2 is $5.9m. The credit phases down from 2030, inside the projection window, and H.R.1/OBBBA (July 2025) severely limits 45X eligibility for products made with 'material assistance from' a foreign entity of concern. Bear 12.5% for 45X impairment plus soft data-centre demand; bull 10.5%.

base.growth_narrative: Y1 +15%: FY2026 capacity ramp to 14GW US (Alabama ramp + Louisiana full-year), CuRe technology launch. Y2 +20%: FY2027 full 14GW + South Carolina finishing facility beginning to contribute, CuRe adders from backlog ($600M through 2028), 45X credits reaching ~$2.4-2.5B. Y3 +15%: US capacity approaching 17.7GW, India volume growth. Y4 +8%: 45X phase-down begins (75% of full credit from 2030), moderation. Y5 +5%: Steady-state deceleration toward terminal.
base.terminal_growth_note: Capped at 2.5% per instructions — mature manufacturing sector with commodity pricing exposure

bull.growth_narrative: Strong Section 232 polysilicon tariff outcome drives US market pricing power and accelerates bookings. ITC TOPCon patent exclusion order reduces competition. 45X credits preserved and growing toward $2.5B+. Southeast Asia capacity fully utilised via SC finishing facility. Perovskite pilot validates next-gen roadmap.

bear.growth_narrative: Partial 45X erosion: future legislation or OBBBA compliance complexity reduces effective credit by 20-30%. Weak 232 outcome; SE Asia stays underutilised with write-downs. Securities class action creates management distraction and potential settlement. Booking pace continues declining (annualised ~7-8GW vs 17-18GW sold) — post-2028 revenue cliff materialises earlier than expected.
bear.terminal_growth_note: Reduced terminal growth reflects post-45X sunset (2032) FCF compression and commoditised module market without subsidy premium

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (1.5-3.5%). Base case at WACC 11%, TG 2.5% = $227.19. Current price $224.57 sits in the WACC 11%/TG 2.5% cell — stock appears approximately fairly valued in base case.

sanity_check_verdict.reason: Weighted IV $116.33 vs $210.1 (-44.6%). The prior +11.5% rested on a $1,200m FCF base against actual H1 FCF of -$639.6m.
sanity_check_verdict.nuance: Even the bull case -- $1,000m normalised FCF, demand holding, 45X intact -- lands at -14.2%. There is no scenario in this rebuild where $210.10 is justified by cash flow rather than by the AI-demand narrative. Note also a new securities class action (June 2026, EDNY) alleging the company understated how US tariff policy would hit 2026 performance, with a derivative suit following in July.
sanity_check_verdict.value_investor_conclusion: AVOID. Ex-subsidy the operations lose money, free cash flow is negative $640m for the half, revenue is declining on contract terminations, and 79% of gross profit comes from a credit that phases down from 2030 and now carries FEOC eligibility restrictions. The growth case rests on the same AI capex cycle being deliberately avoided elsewhere in the portfolio -- and the company quantifies none of it.

key_model_notes: 45X credit dependency: ~75-80% of FY2026 guided EBITDA is the Section 45X manufacturing credit ($2.1-2.2B). This is a LEGISLATIVE SINGLE-POINT-OF-FAILURE — WACC carries a +1.5% premium in base case and +2.5% in bear case to price this structural risk.

Backlog provides revenue visibility through 2030 (47.9 GW / $14.4B contracted as of Q1 2026), but replenishment rate (~7-8 GW/yr new bookings vs 17-18 GW/yr sold) implies post-2028 revenue cliff risk if booking pace does not recover.

45X phase-down in OBBBA: credits reduce to 75% in 2030, 50% in 2031, 25% in 2032, then zero. This drives FCF compression in Y4-Y5 of base case and informs the below-consensus terminal growth rate of 2.5%.

Net cash position of -$2,304.7M (i.e., $2,304.7M net cash) is added to enterprise value, materially boosting intrinsic value vs. a leveraged peer. Total debt is primarily the India manufacturing facility credit ($373.7M) and Indian working capital facilities.

FCF CAGR historically is not computable (negative for FY2016-FY2024 due to deliberate $5B+ capacity expansion). FY2025 $1,187M FCF is the first normalised year; $1,200M DCF base is validated against guided FY2026 EBITDA $2.6-2.8B less guided capex $0.8-1.0B.
Securities class action (filed June 2026) is not explicitly modelled but is subsumed in the bear case via higher WACC and reduced growth expectations.

fields_updated: full model rebuild on Q2-2026 actuals

valuation_philosophy:
Rebuilt 2026-08-28 on Q2-2026; the thesis does not survive it. FOUR findings.

(1) THE BUSINESS IS THE SUBSIDY. Section 45X reduced H1 cost of sales by $862.5m, equal to 79.0% of gross profit and 108.4% of operating income. Strip it and H1 operating income is NEGATIVE $66.8m; Q2 is $5.9m on $1.06bn of sales. The prior research note put this at '~75-80% of EBITDA'; at the operating line the dependency is now total. The credit phases down from 2030 and H.R.1/OBBBA now limits eligibility where there is 'material assistance' from a foreign entity of concern.

(2) CASH DOES NOT FOLLOW EARNINGS. H1 operating cash flow was -$359.8m against $769.2m of net income. The gap is mostly a $649.3m build in government grants receivable -- 45X recognised but not collected. Free cash flow was about -$639.6m.

(3) THE MARGIN BEAT IS ONE-OFF. Gross margin rose to 57.3% from 45.6%, but management attributes it to an $88.6m net IEEPA tariff-refund benefit (the Supreme Court ruled those tariffs unlawful in February 2026 -- a non-recurring refund), higher 45X volume, and lower logistics. Meanwhile REVENUE FELL 3.7% on customer contract terminations despite +5.3% volume, so realised price per watt is deteriorating. Ex-IEEPA, Q2 gross margin is closer to 48.9%.

(4) THE DEMAND STORY IS AI-DEPENDENT, UNQUANTIFIED, AND HEDGED BY THE COMPANY ITSELF. The only data-centre disclosure in the filing attributes rising electric load to 'artificial intelligence-driven data center demand', then immediately warns it 'may be adversely affected by opposition from local communities' over permitting and that data centres 'may address their large energy needs from sources that compete with solar energy, such as on- or off-grid natural gas'. There are NO hyperscaler contracts, no named counterparties and no quantified AI-driven bookings anywhere in the 10-Q. Backlog is 45.1GW / $13.6bn to 2030, an ASP of ~$0.302/W, and contract terminations are recurrent enough to warrant a haircut -- First Solar is suing BP Solar and Lightsource over one.

Offsetting: the balance sheet is strong -- debt cut from $498.8m to $37.6m with long-term debt at zero, and ~$1.69bn net cash. That is why the bear is a de-rating, not distress. But even the bull case here does not reach today's price.
